question.question: Which of the following statements about Amazon S3 storage classes is correct?

options.text: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) is designed for data accessed less than once per month and offers lower storage cost than S3 Standard but higher retrieval cost.
S3 Glacier Deep Archive provides the lowest storage cost but requires a minimum storage duration of 30 days.
S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between two access tiers based on changing access patterns, but does not support S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) stores data across multiple Availability Zones for increased durability.

question.explanation: Option A correctly describes S3 Standard-IA: it targets infrequent access (less than once per month), has lower storage fees than S3 Standard, and incurs higher retrieval charges. Option B is incorrect because S3 Glacier Deep Archive has a minimum storage duration of 180 days, not 30 days. Option C is incorrect because S3 Intelligent-Tiering does support archive access tiers (including Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive). Option D is incorrect because S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, reducing durability compared to multi‑AZ classes.
